model.intro: How good the match model is, shown in the open: every prediction is stored before kick-off and can't be changed afterwards, and every change to the model is tested before it goes live, by a test written before its result was seen.
key: How surprised the model was by what happened, averaged over every match. Lower is better. Giving every match the usual home, draw and away rates scores about 1.07.
The squared gap between the chances given and what happened. Lower is better.
How often the outcome the model made most likely happened.
The model's log loss minus the bookmakers' (their closing prices with the margin taken out). Minus means the model did better.
A change scored on matches played after it was written down, so it can't have been tuned to them.
Green: statistical evidence the change makes the model better. Red: evidence it makes it worse. No colour: not proven either way yet.

clubs.intro: Every club ranked by strength, on a scale where 100 points is worth about a goal a game.
key: A club's long-term level: its rating averaged over roughly its last 100 matches. Slow to move.
Its rating after its latest match. It rises when the club does better than expected, and falls when it does worse.
Current minus Baseline. Green: playing above its usual level. Red: below it.
How far its rating has moved over its last 6 matches.
Its place among every ranked club, by Baseline.
Its place among the clubs in its own league, by Baseline. This is the site's ranking, not the league table.

players.intro: Players ranked by Ability, the model's 0 to 100 estimate of how good each one is now.
key: A 0 to 100 estimate of his level, from the clubs he plays for and his own statistics. An average Premier League regular is about 75. The + shows past and projected seasons.
The role he has started in most over his last 20 appearances.
His place by Ability among every listed player.
His place by Ability among the listed players in his club's league.
Goals and assists this season, for all his clubs.

leagues.intro: Leagues ranked by the average strength of their clubs this season.
key: The average long-term rating of the league's clubs.
The average of its clubs' ratings now.
Current minus Baseline. Green: its clubs are rated above their long-term level. Red: below it.

nations.intro: National teams ranked by strength, worked out from every men's full international since 1872.
key: The team's rating now. 100 points is about one goal a game on a neutral ground.
How far its rating has moved over the last 12 months.
The confederation it plays in. The buttons above the table show one at a time.

matches.intro: Fixtures and results, with the model's chance of a home win, a draw and an away win for each match.
key: The model's chances of a home win, a draw and an away win, as percentages.
The bookmakers' chances for the same match: their odds with the bookmaker's margin taken out, averaged across bookmakers.
The goals the model expects each side to score, such as 1.6–0.9. An average over many possible games, not a score prediction.

stats.intro: How accurate the model's match predictions have been, and how they compare with the bookmakers'. Club and national team matches together: pick a competition to see one on its own.
key: Punishes the model for being confident and wrong. Lower is better. Giving every result a one-in-three chance scores 1.099.
The average squared gap between the chances given and what happened. Lower is better. One-in-three for everything scores 0.667.
How many goals out the projected score was, on average, for each team.
The bookmakers' chances with their margin taken out, averaged across bookmakers, from the last odds before kick-off.
The model's log loss minus the market's. Green (below zero): the model was more accurate. Red: the market was.
The same comparison against the first odds recorded for each match, with the number of matches in brackets.

record.intro: Every prediction the model made, as it was locked before kick-off, beside what happened.
key: Each prediction is stored before the match starts, and the database refuses any change to it afterwards.
The outcome given the highest chance happened.
A hash of the stored prediction: the same prediction always gives the same fingerprint.

lineups.intro: How often the line-ups the model predicted matched the team sheets.
key: Predictions stored before the team sheet came out. The only fair test.
The model run again on past matches, using what was known before each one. A guide, not proof.
Line-ups where all 11 starters were predicted.

tips.intro: Upcoming selections where the model and the bookmakers disagree most. A disagreement isn't a tip: so far the bookmakers have been right more often.
key: The kinds of bet compared: the result, over or under a number of goals, and both teams to score.
The bookmakers' chance for the selection, with their margin taken out.
The share of selections recorded at better odds than the last price before kick-off.
The share of settled selections that won.

research.intro: How the match model is doing, looked at closely: accuracy month by month, whether its chances come true as often as it says, how it compares with the bookmakers in each competition, and every challenger's running score on live matches.
key: How surprised the model was by what happened. Lower is better.
Whether things the model calls 30% happen about 30% of the time. On the diagonal is right.
Model minus bookmakers in log loss on the same matches. Minus means the model was ahead.
The live model's log loss minus the challenger's. Plus is better for the challenger.

changes.intro: Every change to a model that was proposed: what it was expected to do, what testing showed, what was decided, and how it has done since.
key: How surprised the model was by what happened. Lower is better.
The squared distance between the chances given and what happened, summed over home, draw and away. Lower is better.
Better or Worse is said only when a result's interval leaves zero out. A figure with no interval, or one whose interval crosses zero, is Unclear whatever its sign.
A score on the matches a change was built on. It shows the change runs, not that it works.
A score on past matches the change's settings were not chosen on. It is still the past, replayed with today's code.
A score on matches played after the change was fixed, read once at a sample size set beforehand.
How a change deployed to production has done on matches since, worked out from the predictions stored before each kickoff. It is never typed in.
Accepted is a decision. Deployed means the change is in production now. An experiment is never shown as deployed.

bets.intro: A record of those selections as if each had been backed with the same paper stake. No real money is involved.
key: Selections recorded by the nightly update.
Selections recorded shortly before kick-off, after late team news.
The same record without result bets on outsiders.
Over or under 2.5 goals in the match. 1.5, 3.5 and 4.5 work the same way.

efl.intro: Expected Fantasy EFL points for Championship, League One and League Two players and clubs.
key: The points the model expects in that gameweek.
The chance of a clean sheet.
Goalkeeper, defender, midfielder, forward. A * means the position is the site's guess from match data.
A team's shape: one goalkeeper, then defenders, midfielders and forwards.

fpl.intro: Expected Fantasy Premier League points. Shown to the site owner only.

myteam.intro: The site owner's own Fantasy Premier League team and transfer plan.
